1/2 Cup Butter to Grams Converter

How Many Grams in 1/2 Cup of Butter?

This is perhaps the most satisfying conversion in all of baking: ½ cup butter = 1 stick = 8 tablespoons = 113 grams (113.4 g precisely). Unlike flour, which can vary by 25% depending on how you scoop, butter is sold in standardized sticks with the tablespoon markings printed right on the wrapper. You can't really get this one wrong — but it's still helpful to know the exact gram figure when scaling recipes or working from international cookbooks.

The Conversion Formula

Half the full-cup density for each butter state:

  • Grams = Cups × Grams-per-Cup
  • Stick Butter: 0.5 × 227 g = 113 g (113.4 g precisely, 1 stick, 8 tbsp)
  • Melted Butter: 0.5 × 240 g = 120 grams
  • Whipped Butter: 0.5 × 150 g = 75 grams

Stick Butter: The Baker's Shortcut

American butter sticks are brilliantly designed: each stick is exactly ½ cup, and the wax-paper wrapper is printed with lines marking every tablespoon (8 tbsp per stick). If a recipe calls for ½ cup (113 g) of butter, you don't even need a measuring cup — just unwrap one stick and drop it in. For recipes using grams, knowing that 1 stick = 113 g lets you scale effortlessly: 1 tbsp ≈ 14 g, 2 tbsp ≈ 28 g, and so on.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: How many grams is 1/2 cup of butter?

A1: One half cup of standard stick butter weighs exactly 113 grams (113.4 g precisely). That's one full US stick or 8 tablespoons — the most reliable conversion in baking.

Q2: Is 1/2 cup of butter equal to 1 stick?

A2: Yes. ½ cup = 1 standard American stick = 113.4 grams = 8 tablespoons. Most wrappers have tablespoon markings, so you can measure without any tools at all.

Q3: What if my butter is melted — does 1/2 cup still equal 113 g?

A3: No. Melted butter is denser: a full ½ cup of already-melted butter weighs ~120 grams. If a recipe says "½ cup butter, melted," measure 1 stick (113 g) solid first, then melt it — don't pour melted butter to the ½ cup line.
